# integration-matter

A [MajorDom](https://majordom.io) integration — bridges **Matter** (CSA Connectivity Standard)
devices into the MajorDom language.

Built for the **MajorDom Hub**, but it doesn't need it: this is a standalone, standardized
library for Matter that you can use on its own (see **Run it standalone** below). Built on the
[MajorDom Integration SDK](https://github.com/MajorDom-Systems/integration-sdk). The entry point
is `MatterController` (`majordom_matter/controller.py`), which the Hub — or the SDK's dev runner —
instantiates and drives through its lifecycle: discovery → pairing → commands → teardown.

- **Other protocols:** browse the [MajorDom integrations](https://github.com/orgs/MajorDom-Systems/repositories?q=integration-).
- **Create your own:** start from the [integration template](https://github.com/MajorDom-Systems/integration-template).

## Documentation

Full integration-author docs — the controller lifecycle, data models, storing data, discovery,
and a worked example — live at **[docs.majordom.io](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration)**.

## Development

```sh
poetry install && poetry run poe install
```

| Task | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `poe check` | Full quality pipeline (ruff, ty, pytest, poetry build/check) |
| `poe check --ci` | Same, plus `git diff --exit-code` |

Work lands on `develop`; `master` is protected and released via **Actions → Release**. The default
suite drives the controller against a canned node with the SDK's test doubles — no matter-server,
no docker (`tests/test_controller_stub.py`). The exhaustive real-device coverage commissions
Google's Matter Virtual Devices in a dockerized matter-server (`tests/test_controller.py`, see
`docker-compose.matter-tests.yml`); the MVD binaries + PAA certs are fetched, not committed.

## Run it standalone (without the Hub)

`majordom-matter` is a standalone library — import it into your own app, or run **just this
integration** interactively (discover, pair, control, and inspect devices from a prompt) with no Hub.
It needs a running [python-matter-server](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/python-matter-server)
reachable over its WebSocket (`MATTER_SERVER_URL`, default `ws://localhost:5580/ws`); Thread devices
also need an OpenThread Border Router.

See **[Standalone mode](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration/standalone)** for the interactive
CLI, watch mode, and the programmatic API.

## About this integration

- **Protocol / platform:** Matter (Connectivity Standards Alliance) via `python-matter-server` + `chip`.
- **Transport(s):** IP over Thread / Wi-Fi / Ethernet; BLE for commissioning.
- **Supported devices:** any Matter-certified device — lights, plugs, switches, sensors, locks,
  thermostats, covers, fans, appliances (verified against 30 Matter Virtual Device types).
- **Credentials needed to pair:** `code` (manual pairing code) or `qr`.

### Required harness

- **Hardware adapters:** an 802.15.4 radio (e.g. a SkyConnect / Thread dongle) for Thread devices —
  driven by matter-server / the OTBR, not this package directly.
- **Third-party software services:** a **matter-server** instance reachable over WebSocket
  (`MATTER_SERVER_URL`), and an **OpenThread Border Router (OTBR)** for Thread devices.
- **OS / permissions:** BLE access for commissioning; mDNS on the LAN for on-network discovery.

### Protocol stack (OSI)

| OSI layer | Protocol | Implemented by |
|-----------|----------|----------------|
| Application (7) | Matter clusters / data model | **this integration** (via `chip` lib) |
| Session (5) | CASE / PASE secure session | library (matter-server) |
| Transport (4) | UDP | OS |
| Network (3) | IPv6 · 6LoWPAN | OS · OTBR (harness) |
| Data link / Physical (1–2) | Thread · IEEE 802.15.4 (or Wi-Fi / Ethernet) | radio adapter (harness) |

### Progress

- [x] Discovery services registered (mDNS on-network via matter-server; BLE for commissionable devices); cancel closures called in `stop`
- [x] Discovery listeners fire and call `controller_did_receive_discovery`
- [x] Re-discovery of already-paired devices on reconnect (`controller_did_connect_device`)
- [x] Device pairing (BLE→Thread and on-network commissioning)
- [x] Device schema mapped: device info, parameter list, per-parameter metadata → MajorDom's domain model
- [x] Hub → Device control (`send_command`)
- [x] Device → Hub event subscription (`controller_did_receive_events`)
- [x] `identify`
- [x] `unpair`
- [x] `fetch`
- [x] Availability tracking while running (`controller_did_lose_device` / `last_error`)
- [x] Graceful shutdown in `stop`
- [x] Tests pass against virtual/simulated devices (stub + dockerized MVD suite)
- [x] Owned — maintained by Parker Industries

### Parameter metadata sources & priority

Every parameter's UX metadata is resolved from several sources.
See also the [parameter-ux recipe](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration/parameter-ux).

**Visibility / role / unit** — resolved by `classify_attribute()` in `matter_spec.py` (first match wins):

| # | Source | What it is |
|---|--------|-----------|
| — | system cluster / sensitive (`Aliro*` crypto) | forced **system** (safety, top priority) |
| 1 | `OUR_ATTRIBUTE_UX` (`USER_READINGS`, `EVERYDAY_CONTROL_ATTRIBUTES`) | our hand curation |
| 2 | `MATTER_HA_ATTRIBUTE_UX` | judgment **harvested** from Home Assistant's Matter discovery (`scripts/harvest_matter_ha.py`, AST-parsed, vendored — no `homeassistant` dep) |
| 3 | **fallback policy** | writable → setting, else system; **logs a warning** on uncurated attrs. Flip `_FALLBACK_HIDE_UNCURATED` once coverage is validated. |

Matter has no runtime quirk layer, so (unlike zigbee) there is no v2-quirk tier. The Matter Data
Model (`chip`) already supplies names/types/bounds; the harvest adds only the `entity_category`
(user/config/diagnostic) judgment the spec doesn't dictate.

**Bounds** come from the device's own limit attributes (runtime) > spec tables > wire-type range —
see `resolve_runtime_bounds()` / `METADATA_SOURCES`.

**Drift.** `scripts/check_matter_ha_drift.py` re-runs the AST harvest against home-assistant/core and
diffs vs the vendored artifact via the SDK's `diff_specs`, tiering ADD / REMOVE / **RECLASSIFY**.

### Notes

The MVD `chef` binaries are x86-64 Linux only, so the real-device suite runs in an amd64 container
(Rosetta on Apple Silicon). A monthly canary fetches the *latest* upstream MVD release and fails if
it ships something unsupported — the signal to add support. The same drift machinery (the SDK's
`diff_specs`) now also watches the harvested HA-Matter judgment.

## License

See [LICENSE](LICENSE). For commercial licensing or partnership inquiries regarding MajorDom,
contact us via [parker-industries.org/partnership](https://parker-industries.org/partnership).

# FILE: docker/Dockerfile.test
================================================================================
# Runs the Matter integration's virtual-device suite against real MVD `chef` binaries.
# Build context is the repo root; the SDK is a published PyPI dependency
# (majordom-integration-sdk), resolved by `poetry install` — nothing is copied from outside the repo.
FROM python:3.13-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential gcc python3-dev git \
    avahi-daemon avahi-utils libavahi-client3 libavahi-common3 \
    dbus libdbus-1-3 libdbus-1-dev libglib2.0-0 libglib2.0-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN sed -i 's/#enable-dbus=yes/enable-dbus=no/g;  s/use-ipv6=no/use-ipv6=yes/g; s/#enable-chroot=yes/enable-chroot=no/g' \
    /etc/avahi/avahi-daemon.conf

RUN pip install poetry && poetry config virtualenvs.create false

COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock /app/
RUN poetry install --no-root

COPY . /app/
RUN pip install -e . --no-deps

CMD avahi-daemon --daemonize && sleep 2 && \
    chmod +x tests/mvd/* && \
    poetry run pytest tests/ -v

# FILE: docker-compose.matter-tests.mac.yml

# macOS (Apple-silicon) override: the MVD binaries are Linux x86-64, so pin the test
# container to linux/amd64 and let Docker Desktop's Rosetta run them.
# One-time: Docker Desktop -> Settings -> General -> "Use Rosetta for x86/amd64 emulation".
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.matter-tests.yml -f docker-compose.matter-tests.mac.yml \
#     up --build --exit-code-from matter-integration-tests
# matter-server runs no x86-64 binary (just mDNS/network), so it stays native arm64.
services:
  matter-integration-tests:
    platform: linux/amd64
    environment:
      - MATTER_DISCOVERY_WARMUP_S=180

# FILE: docker-compose.matter-tests.yml
================================================================================
# Matter integration test stack: python-matter-server + a container that runs the
# integration's virtual-device suite against real MVD `chef` binaries.
#
# Run:  docker compose -f docker-compose.matter-tests.yml up --build \
#         --exit-code-from matter-integration-tests
# On Apple Silicon add the mac override (Rosetta):  -f docker-compose.matter-tests.mac.yml
services:
  matter-server:
    image: ghcr.io/matter-js/python-matter-server:stable
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    sysctls:
      - net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=0
      - net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
    volumes:
      - ./matter_data:/data
    command: --storage-path /data --paa-root-cert-dir /data/credentials --primary-interface eth0
    networks: [matter-net]

  matter-integration-tests:
    build:
      context: .             # repo root; the SDK is a published PyPI dependency
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile.test
    privileged: true
    depends_on: [matter-server]
    environment:
      - MATTER_SERVER_URL=ws://matter-server:5580  # the base URL: the suite adds /ws
      - MATTER_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_S=12
      - MATTER_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1
    sysctls:
      - net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=0
    networks: [matter-net]

networks:
  matter-net:
    driver: bridge
    enable_ipv6: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.16.238.0/24
        - subnet: fd00:db8:1::/64


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_matter/__init__.py
================================================================================
"""Matter integration for MajorDom.

Bridges Matter devices into the MajorDom language via matterjs-server, through the python-matter-server client.
`peripherals` is what the Hub (or the SDK's standalone dev runner) runs: matterjs-server and the
`MatterController` that drives it.
"""

from majordom_integration_sdk import Peripheral, Platform

from majordom_matter.config import matterjs_server
from majordom_matter.controller import MatterController


def peripherals(platform: Platform) -> list[Peripheral]:
    return [matterjs_server(), MatterController(platform)]


__all__ = ["MatterController", "peripherals"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_matter/ble_delegate.py
================================================================================
"""Lends the hub's Bluetooth to matterjs-server, so commissioning reaches devices through every radio
the Bluetooth router (``ble/router``) hears with — local adapters and ESPHome nodes alike.

matterjs-server (``BLE_PROXY=true``) takes a Bluetooth client on ``/ble`` and drives it with the
BLE proxy protocol v1: https://github.com/matter-js/matterjs-server/blob/main/docs/ble-proxy-protocol.md
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import contextlib
import json
import logging
import struct
from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from uuid import UUID

from aiohttp import ClientSession, ClientWebSocketResponse, WSMsgType
from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import BLEConnection, BLEDiscoveryInfo, BLEMatcher, BLERouter

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_FRAME = struct.Struct(">BH")  # opcode, connection handle; the payload follows
_WRITE, _NOTIFICATION = 0x01, 0x02
_RECONNECT_SEC, _RECONNECT_MAX_SEC = 1, 10  # the first retry, then doubling up to the most


class _Failure(Exception):
    def __init__(self, error: str, message: str = ""):
        super().__init__(message or error)
        self.error = error


@dataclass
class _Peripheral:
    connection: BLEConnection
    lease: contextlib.AsyncExitStack  # holds the Bluetooth source leased for this connection
    characteristics: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)  # uuid -> handle
    write_handle: int | None = None  # where binary frames go: the characteristic last written


def _uuid(text: str) -> UUID:
    """Short (``fff6``), 32-bit or full UUID text as a UUID."""
    return UUID(text.rjust(8, "0") + "-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb" if len(text) <= 8 else text)


def _b64(data: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.b64encode(data).decode()


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _gatt(error: str) -> Generator[None]:
    """Answers a failing GATT operation as ``error``, however its source failed (bleak, aioesphomeapi, a lost link)."""
    try:
        yield
    except Exception as e:
        raise _Failure(error, str(e)) from e


class MatterServerBLEDelegate:
    """Connects to matterjs-server's ``/ble`` endpoint and performs its BLE operations through the Bluetooth router.

    It reconnects whenever matterjs-server goes away. Run one per matterjs-server.
    """

    def __init__(self, url: str, ble: BLERouter, session: ClientSession):
        self._url, self._ble, self._session = url, ble, session
        self._ws: ClientWebSocketResponse | None = None
        self._peripherals: dict[int, _Peripheral] = {}
        self._last_handle = 0
        self._stop_scanning: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()

    async def run(self):
        """Serves matterjs-server until cancelled, reconnecting whenever it goes away."""
        delay = _RECONNECT_SEC
        while True:
            try:
                async with self._session.ws_connect(self._url) as ws:
                    self._ws = ws
                    if await self._serve(ws):
                        delay = _RECONNECT_SEC
                reason = "closed"
            except Exception as e:  # whatever broke, matterjs-server must get the hub's Bluetooth back
                reason = f"failed: {e!r}"
            finally:
                await self._release()
            log = logger.warning if delay == _RECONNECT_SEC else logger.debug  # once per outage, not every retry
            log(f"matterjs-server's /ble endpoint {self._url} {reason}, reconnecting in {delay} s")
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            delay = min(delay * 2, _RECONNECT_MAX_SEC)

    async def _serve(self, ws: ClientWebSocketResponse) -> bool:
        """Serves one connection until it closes; False when matterjs-server refuses it."""
        await ws.send_json({"type": "hello", "version": 1})
        if error := (await ws.receive_json(timeout=10)).get("error"):
            logger.warning(f"matterjs-server refused the hub's Bluetooth: {error}")
            return False
        logger.info(f"Lending Bluetooth to matterjs-server at {self._url}")
        async for message in ws:
            if message.type == WSMsgType.TEXT:
                self._spawn(self._answer(ws, json.loads(message.data)))
            elif message.type == WSMsgType.BINARY:
                await self._forward(message.data)  # in order: these are segments of one stream
        return True

    async def _answer(self, ws: ClientWebSocketResponse, command: dict):
        try:
            handler = getattr(self, f"_{command['command']}", None)
            if not handler:
                raise _Failure("internal_error", f"Unknown command {command['command']}")
            result = await handler(**command.get("args", {}))
            reply = {"id": command["id"], "success": True, "result": result or {}}
        except Exception as e:
            error = e.error if isinstance(e, _Failure) else "internal_error"
            reply = {"id": command["id"], "success": False, "error": error, "message": str(e)}
        await ws.send_json(reply)

    async def _forward(self, frame: bytes):
        opcode, handle = _FRAME.unpack_from(frame)
        peripheral = self._peripherals.get(handle)
        if opcode == _WRITE and peripheral and peripheral.write_handle is not None:
            try:
                await peripheral.connection.write(
                    peripheral.write_handle, frame[_FRAME.size :], is_response_needed=True
                )
            except Exception as e:  # a BTP segment is no request to fail, and BTP can't skip one: end the connection
                logger.warning(f"Bluetooth write on connection {handle} failed, disconnecting: {e!r}")
                self._lost(handle)
                self._spawn(self._close(peripheral))

    def _peripheral(self, connection_handle: int) -> _Peripheral:
        if peripheral := self._peripherals.get(connection_handle):
            return peripheral
        raise _Failure("not_connected")

    def _characteristic(self, connection_handle: int, uuid: str) -> tuple[_Peripheral, int]:
        peripheral = self._peripheral(connection_handle)
        if (handle := peripheral.characteristics.get(uuid.lower())) is None:
            raise _Failure("characteristic_not_found", uuid)
        return peripheral, handle

    # Commands

    async def _start_scan(self, service_uuids: list[str] | None = None, allow_duplicates: bool = False):
        await self._stop_scan()
        self._stop_scanning = self._ble.register(
            self, [BLEMatcher(_uuid(u)) for u in service_uuids or ()] or [BLEMatcher()]
        )

    async def _stop_scan(self):
        if self._stop_scanning:
            self._stop_scanning()
            self._stop_scanning = None

    async def _connect(self, address: str, timeout: int = 30_000):
        self._last_handle = handle = self._last_handle % 0xFFFF + 1
        async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:  # closed here on failure, kept for the connection otherwise
            try:
                lease = await stack.enter_async_context(
                    self._ble.exclusive(address, owner="matter", timeout=timeout / 1000)
                )
                connection = await asyncio.wait_for(lease.connect(lambda: self._lost(handle)), timeout / 1000)
            except TimeoutError as e:
                raise _Failure("timeout") from e
            except ConnectionError as e:  # incl. BLEBusyError: every source that hears the device is leased
                raise _Failure("connection_failed", str(e)) from e
            self._peripherals[handle] = _Peripheral(connection, stack.pop_all())
        return {"connection_handle": handle, "mtu": connection.mtu}

    async def _disconnect(self, connection_handle: int):
        peripheral = self._peripheral(connection_handle)
        del self._peripherals[connection_handle]
        await self._close(peripheral)

    async def _discover_services(self, connection_handle: int):
        peripheral = self._peripheral(connection_handle)
        with _gatt("discovery_failed"):
            services = await peripheral.connection.services()
        return {"services": [{"uuid": s.uuid} for s in services]}

    async def _discover_characteristics(self, connection_handle: int, service_uuid: str):
        peripheral = self._peripheral(connection_handle)
        with _gatt("discovery_failed"):
            services = await peripheral.connection.services()
        service = next((s for s in services if _uuid(s.uuid) == _uuid(service_uuid)), None)
        if not service:
            raise _Failure("service_not_found", service_uuid)
        peripheral.characteristics |= {c.uuid.lower(): c.handle for c in service.characteristics}
        return {
            "characteristics": [{"uuid": c.uuid, "properties": list(c.properties)} for c in service.characteristics]
        }

    async def _read_characteristic(self, connection_handle: int, characteristic_uuid: str):
        peripheral, handle = self._characteristic(connection_handle, characteristic_uuid)
        with _gatt("read_failed"):
            return {"value": _b64(await peripheral.connection.read(handle))}

    async def _write_characteristic(
        self, connection_handle: int, characteristic_uuid: str, value: str, response: bool = False
    ):
        peripheral, handle = self._characteristic(connection_handle, characteristic_uuid)
        peripheral.write_handle = handle
        with _gatt("write_failed"):
            await peripheral.connection.write(handle, base64.b64decode(value), response)

    async def _subscribe_characteristic(self, connection_handle: int, characteristic_uuid: str):
        peripheral, handle = self._characteristic(connection_handle, characteristic_uuid)
        with _gatt("subscribe_failed"):
            await peripheral.connection.start_notify(handle, lambda data: self._notify(connection_handle, data))

    async def _write_and_subscribe(
        self,
        connection_handle: int,
        write_uuid: str,
        write_value: str,
        subscribe_uuid: str,
        write_response: bool = True,
    ):
        # the write must complete before notifications are on: the device answers the write by notifying
        await self._write_characteristic(connection_handle, write_uuid, write_value, write_response)
        await self._subscribe_characteristic(connection_handle, subscribe_uuid)

    async def _unsubscribe_characteristic(self, connection_handle: int, characteristic_uuid: str):
        peripheral, handle = self._characteristic(connection_handle, characteristic_uuid)
        await peripheral.connection.stop_notify(handle)

    async def _request_mtu(self, connection_handle: int, mtu: int):
        return {"mtu": self._peripheral(connection_handle).connection.mtu}

    # Events

    async def ble_did_discover_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo):
        adv = info.advertisement
        await self._send_event("device_discovered", {
            "address": info.device.address,
            "connectable": True,  # bleak doesn't say; matterjs-server ignores devices that aren't
            "name": adv.local_name,
            "rssi": adv.rssi,
            "service_uuids": adv.service_uuids,
            "service_data": {uuid: _b64(data) for uuid, data in adv.service_data.items()},
            "manufacturer_data": {str(company): _b64(data) for company, data in adv.manufacturer_data.items()},
        })  # fmt: skip

    ble_did_update_device = ble_did_discover_device

    async def ble_did_remove_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo): ...

    def _notify(self, connection_handle: int, data: bytes):
        if self._ws and not self._ws.closed:
            self._spawn(self._ws.send_bytes(_FRAME.pack(_NOTIFICATION, connection_handle) + data))

    def _lost(self, connection_handle: int):
        if peripheral := self._peripherals.pop(connection_handle, None):
            self._spawn(peripheral.lease.aclose())
            self._spawn(self._send_event("disconnected", {"connection_handle": connection_handle}))

    async def _send_event(self, event: str, data: dict):
        if self._ws and not self._ws.closed:
            await self._ws.send_json({"event": event, "data": data})

    async def _release(self):
        for task in self._tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await self._stop_scan()
        peripherals, self._peripherals = list(self._peripherals.values()), {}
        await asyncio.gather(*(self._close(p) for p in peripherals), return_exceptions=True)

    @staticmethod
    async def _close(peripheral: _Peripheral):
        """Ends the connection and gives its Bluetooth source back, whatever the disconnect does."""
        try:
            await peripheral.connection.disconnect()
        finally:
            await peripheral.lease.aclose()

    def _spawn(self, coroutine):
        task = asyncio.create_task(coroutine)
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._on_task_done)

    def _on_task_done(self, task: asyncio.Task):
        self._tasks.discard(task)
        if not task.cancelled() and (e := task.exception()):
            logger.debug(f"Bluetooth delegate task failed: {e!r}")

# FILE: majordom_matter/client.py

from typing import override

from matter_server.client import MatterClient as _MatterClient
from matter_server.common.models import EventMessage, EventType


class MatterClient(_MatterClient):
    @override
    def _handle_event_message(self, msg: EventMessage):
        # matterjs-server may report a just-commissioned node's attributes before announcing the node (whose
        # announcement carries them). Upstream raises KeyError on those, which ends listening and cancels the
        # commissioning call that's still waiting for its result.
        if msg.event == EventType.ATTRIBUTE_UPDATED and msg.data[0] not in self._nodes:
            return
        super()._handle_event_message(msg)

# FILE: majordom_matter/config.py

"""matterjs-server: the Matter controller service this integration drives over its WebSocket API (``/ws``), lending it
the hub's Bluetooth over its BLE proxy endpoint (``/ble``)."""

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, Need, Service


def matterjs_server() -> Service:
    """matterjs-server, a new one for each runtime."""
    return Service(
        "matterjs-server",
        # Thread is optional: without a border router Matter still works over Wi-Fi and Ethernet. Bluetooth too: an
        # adapter of its own only when no Bluetooth router holds them (disabled, failed or absent). The router is an
        # in-process object a container can't bind: it reaches matterjs-server through the controller (ble_delegate,
        # over /ble) instead.
        needs=[Need("ip"), Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"], is_required=False), Need("ble", ["bluez"], is_required=False)],
        # the base URL: /ws, /ble; "adapter" tells the controller whether an adapter is bound here (empty: none)
        provides=[
            Endpoint(
                "matter", "matter-server", "ws://127.0.0.1:{ports.api}", params={"adapter": "{peripherals.ble.url}"}
            )
        ],
        ports={"api": 5580},
        compose={
            # :dev pinned by digest (2026-10-08); bump on purpose
            "image": "ghcr.io/matter-js/matterjs-server@sha256:bcaacf6b2b2df9ce2b929ad7469d5380a4d627f05f790e201d127e8b65af5b0e",  # noqa: E501
            "network_mode": "host",
            "userns_mode": "host",
            "user": "{host.uid}:{host.gid}",  # its data folder belongs to the hub
            "environment": {
                "STORAGE_PATH": "/data",
                "PORT": "{ports.api}",
                # on the host network, with no authentication: anyone on the LAN could drive the fabric. Loopback
                # unless the host opens its services to the LAN (a lab harness)
                "LISTEN_ADDRESS": "{host.listen_address}",
                # Bluetooth comes from the hub (see ble_delegate) unless an adapter is bound to it. Then noble
                # drives it through the host's BlueZ over the system bus: its default HCI socket backend needs root
                "BLE_PROXY": "{peripherals.ble.url:!true}",
                "BLUETOOTH_ADAPTER": "{peripherals.ble.params[index]}",
                "NOBLE_BINDINGS": "{peripherals.ble.url:?dbus}",
                # matter.js logs every command's fields at info, the Thread network key included
                "LOG_LEVEL": "warning",
            },
            "volumes": [
                "{data}:/data",
                # the system bus only with an adapter: gone without one
                "{peripherals.ble.url:?/run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro}",
            ],
        },
    )

import asyncio
import contextlib
import inspect
import logging
from collections.abc import Coroutine, Generator
from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Any, override
from uuid import UUID

from aiohttp import ClientError, ClientSession
from chip.clusters.ClusterObjects import ClusterAttributeDescriptor, ClusterCommand
from chip.clusters.Objects import ClosureControl, Identify, OperationalState
from majordom_integration_sdk import (
    STABLE_RUN,
    AbstractController,
    IntegrationError,
    Need,
    NoSettings,
    PeripheralChange,
    Platform,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import BLE_ROUTER, BLEDiscoveryInfo, BLERouter
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.base import NonEmptyStr
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.command import DeviceCommand
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import CredentialsType, Discovery, ParameterState, ProvidedCredentials
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import DeviceParameterChange
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterDataType, ParameterRole, ParameterVisibility
from matter_server.client.exceptions import InvalidState, NotConnected, TransportError
from matter_server.client.models.node import MatterNode
from matter_server.common.errors import UnknownError

from majordom_matter.ble_delegate import MatterServerBLEDelegate
from majordom_matter.client import MatterClient

from .exceptions import (
    MatterConnectionError,
    MatterNotFoundParameter,
    MatterUnexpectedError,
    MatterUnsupportedParameter,
)
from .mapper import MatterMapper
from .matter_spec import (
    CLOSURE_MAIN_STATE,
    MAIN_PARAMETER_BY_CLUSTER,
    STATE_TOGGLE_ATTRIBUTES,
    STATE_TOGGLE_COMMANDS,
    AttributeKey,
    DefaultParams,
    MainParameterSpec,
